items.source: Univ. of Bath · Management, Specialist and Administration
items.summary: The Department of Student Support & Safeguarding is a collaborative and student-focused team dedicated to enhancing the student experience through innovative and sector-leading support practices. Working within a multidisciplinary environment, the Mental Health & Wellbeing Service collaborates closely with Therapeutic Services, Disability Services, Money Advice, and Student Retention & Success teams to provide a holistic and integrated response to student needs. We are looking to recruit Mental Health & Wellbeing Practitioners. About the role We are seeking an organised, experienced, and creative registered Mental Health & Wellbeing Professional to join our team and provide quality support to students experiencing mental health and wellbeing challenges. items.title: AstraZeneca Non-Clinical PhD Studentship in Next-generation TPD for oncology: Harnessing ubiquitin-independent pathways
items.summary: The Department of Pharmacology at the University of Cambridge, in partnership with AstraZeneca, is offering a funded PhD studentship to study proteasome-targeting tools and use them to design novel approaches for Targeted Protein Degradation (TPD). We are seeking a motivated and curiosity-driven student with a strong interest in cell biology and biochemistry, as well as an enthusiasm for TPD approaches. The successful candidate will join the lab of Dr Catherine Lindon in the Department of Pharmacology, with a supervisory team that includes Dr Gustavo Gutierrez (Discovery Sciences, AstraZeneca), Professor Laura Itzhaki (Department of Pharmacology), Dr Sharan Bagal (Oncology Chemistry, AstraZeneca) and Dr David McGarry (Oncology Bioscience, AstraZeneca). items.title: Research Assistant (1126-367)
items.source: Royal Holloway · Department of Biological Sciences
items.summary: Full-Time, Fixed-Term (5 months) Applications are invited for the post of Research Assistant in the Department of Biological Sciences. This is a fixed term post for 5 months in the first instance with potential for extension. Joining the Popplewell team at an exciting phase of growth and investment, this appointment will contribute to the development of gene addition therapies for Neurofibromatosis type 1, a childhood disease caused by the lack of neurofibromin that results in Schwann cell proliferation and neurofibroma growth in the peripheral and central nervous system. Building on strong preliminary data from the lab, the successful candidate will work with a senior post-doctoral research associate to further optimise the replacement NF1 cDNA to facilitate cell-specific and responsive expression of neurofibromin. items.title: Research Assistant (0.6 FTE) (EPH-EPED-2026-10)
items.source: LSHTM · Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology and Dynamics
items.summary: The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice. The post-holder will be a member of the team delivering the Lancet Commission: ‘Rethinking Misinformation, Health and Human Security’, led by Prof. Heidi Larson. The Commission comprises an international group of Commissioners to develop approaches addressing misinformation. Working closely with the Commission co-chairs /working group (WG) leads, the post-holder will provide research, analytical and coordination support, alongside stakeholder engagement and dissemination of findings.
